subject: social_science

concepts.title: Money as a Medium of Exchange
concepts.section: MONEY AS A MEDIUM OF EXCHANGE
concepts.definition: Money functions as an intermediate instrument in trade transactions, eliminating the requirement where both trading partners must simultaneously desire each other's goods.
concepts.key_idea: Eliminating double coincidence of wants by acting as a universal medium for trade.
question_patterns: explain how money acts as a medium of exchange
what is meant by double coincidence of wants
how does the introduction of money simplify trade compared to barter
why is direct barter inconvenient in modern transactions
describe the role of money in eliminating barter friction

solution_steps.explain: In barter system both parties must agree to sell and buy each other commodities which is double coincidence of wants
Money acts as an intermediate asset allowing separate selling and purchasing operations in the market

concepts.title: Modern Forms of Money and Demand Deposits
concepts.definition: Modern currency comprises paper notes and coins authorized by the central government, along with demand deposits held in bank accounts that can be transferred via cheques.
concepts.key_idea: Legal tender currency and withdrawable bank deposits constitute modern money.
question_patterns: why are demand deposits considered a form of money
what entity issues currency notes in India on behalf of the central government
explain the mechanism and significance of payments made through cheques
why is modern paper currency accepted as a medium of exchange despite having no intrinsic value
describe the features that distinguish modern money from early forms like cattle or metallic coins

solution_steps.explain: The Reserve Bank of India issues currency authorized by central government making it legal tender that cannot be refused
Bank deposits can be withdrawn on demand and transferred using cheques to settle payments without physical cash

concepts.title: Bank Cash Reserve and Loanable Funds Calculation
concepts.definition: Banks hold a mandatory percentage of customer deposits as cash reserves for daily withdrawals and deploy the remaining fraction as loans to borrowers.
concepts.key_idea: Determining the cash held by banks and the surplus balance extended as credit.
question_patterns: calculate the cash reserves held by a bank given total deposits of {total_deposits} and reserve ratio of {reserve_percentage} percent
find the amount of loans a bank can extend from total deposits of {total_deposits} with cash reserve ratio {reserve_percentage} percent
a bank receives {total_deposits} in deposits and keeps {reserve_percentage} percent as cash reserve find the loanable funds
determine how much cash reserve a bank must keep if total deposits are {total_deposits} and reserve requirement is {reserve_percentage} percent
what is the loanable amount available to a bank with {total_deposits} deposits and {reserve_percentage} percent reserve ratio

solution_steps.explain: Multiply total deposits by cash reserve percentage divided by 100
Subtract cash reserve from total deposits to get available loan balance

concepts.title: Net Interest Income of Commercial Banks
concepts.definition: The primary income source for commercial banks is the spread between interest collected from borrowers and interest paid out to depositors.
concepts.key_idea: Calculating bank profit from the difference between lending interest and deposit interest.
question_patterns: calculate the net income of a bank that lends {loan_amount} at {borrower_rate} percent and pays {depositor_rate} percent on {deposit_amount} deposits
find the main earnings of a bank collecting {borrower_rate} percent on {loan_amount} loans and giving {depositor_rate} percent on {deposit_amount} deposits
determine the net interest profit when a bank lends {loan_amount} at {borrower_rate} percent interest and pays {depositor_rate} percent on {deposit_amount}
how much income does a bank make if loan interest rate is {borrower_rate} percent on {loan_amount} and deposit interest rate is {depositor_rate} percent on {deposit_amount}
what is the net bank income from {loan_amount} lent at {borrower_rate} percent and {deposit_amount} deposited at {depositor_rate} percent

solution_steps.explain: Multiply total loan amount by borrower interest rate divided by 100
Multiply total deposit amount by depositor interest rate divided by 100
Subtract interest paid from interest received to obtain main bank income

concepts.title: Credit Impact and Debt Trap Dynamics
concepts.definition: Credit can either enhance earnings when used productively for capital needs or push borrowers into a cycle of persistent debt when crop or enterprise failure occurs.
concepts.key_idea: Credit acts as a growth catalyst in positive scenarios or leads to a debt trap under high-risk failures.
question_patterns: compare how credit produced different outcomes for Salim and Swapna
what is a debt trap and under what conditions does a borrower fall into it
explain how credit can play a positive role in business development
why is crop production in rural areas considered high risk for credit repayment
describe the key factors that determine whether borrowing will leave a person better or worse off

solution_steps.explain: In favorable situations credit satisfies working capital needs enabling timely production and higher earnings
In high risk cases like crop failure repayment becomes impossible forcing borrowers to sell assets or take new loans

concepts.title: Terms of Credit and Collateral Requirements
concepts.definition: Terms of credit comprise the agreed interest rate, collateral security, documentation requirements, and the specified repayment schedule between lender and borrower.
concepts.key_idea: Collateral and terms dictate eligibility, cost, and risk in credit agreements.
question_patterns: what are the four essential components comprising terms of credit
define collateral and explain why formal lenders demand it before granting loans
how do terms of credit vary between formal banks and informal village lenders
why do poor households struggle to meet bank documentation and collateral conditions
explain the role of house or land papers as collateral in long term bank loans

solution_steps.explain: Collateral is an asset owned by the borrower that serves as security guarantee to the lender until repayment
Terms of credit include interest rate collateral documentation requirement and mode of repayment

concepts.title: Formal and Informal Credit Sectors and RBI Supervision
concepts.definition: Formal credit from banks and cooperatives is supervised by the Reserve Bank of India to ensure fair rates and targeted social lending, unlike unregulated informal credit.
concepts.key_idea: Formal sector credit offers lower interest rates under RBI regulation whereas informal sector lacks oversight.
question_patterns: distinguish between formal sector and informal sector sources of credit in India
how does the Reserve Bank of India supervise formal commercial banks
why is cheap and affordable credit critical for national economic development
why do rich urban households rely mostly on formal credit while poor households depend on informal credit
explain why expanding formal credit in rural areas is necessary to reduce exploitation

solution_steps.explain: Formal sector comprises banks and cooperatives with lower interest rates while informal sector includes moneylenders charging high rates
RBI monitors minimum cash reserves lending priorities to small borrowers and interest rate reporting

concepts.title: Self-Help Groups and Rural Microfinance
concepts.definition: Self-Help Groups aggregate small savings of poor community members, particularly women, to extend low-interest loans and build bank eligibility without individual collateral.
concepts.key_idea: Community savings pooling enables collective credit access and social empowerment without traditional collateral.
question_patterns: explain the basic functioning and organizational structure of a Self Help Group
how do Self Help Groups solve the problem of lack of collateral for poor borrowers
what role do group members play in deciding loan terms within a Self Help Group
discuss the impact of microcredit initiatives like Grameen Bank of Bangladesh on poor women
how do Self Help Groups contribute to social empowerment beyond financial assistance

solution_steps.explain: 15 to 20 members pool small savings regularly to provide low interest loans for internal community needs
Regular saving enables the group to secure bank loans in the group name without requiring individual asset collateral

worked_examples.question_pattern: A bank receives total deposits of 100000 rupees and keeps 5 percent as cash reserve. Calculate the cash reserve and the remaining loanable funds.

solution_template.explain: Multiply total deposits by cash reserve percentage divided by 100
Subtract cash reserve from total deposits to get available loan balance

worked_examples.question_pattern: If a commercial bank holds 500000 rupees in deposits and maintains a reserve ratio of 10 percent, find the total loanable amount.

solution_template.explain: Multiply total deposits by cash reserve percentage divided by 100
Subtract cash reserve from total deposits to get available loan balance

worked_examples.question_pattern: A bank extends loans of 80000 rupees at 12 percent annual interest and holds deposits of 100000 rupees paying 4 percent annual interest. Calculate the bank's net annual interest income.

solution_template.explain: Multiply total loan amount by borrower interest rate divided by 100
Multiply total deposit amount by depositor interest rate divided by 100
Subtract interest paid from interest received to obtain main bank income

worked_examples.question_pattern: Calculate the net profit earned by a bank lending 200000 rupees at 10 percent interest while paying 5 percent interest on 200000 rupees of deposits.

solution_template.explain: Multiply total loan amount by borrower interest rate divided by 100
Multiply total deposit amount by depositor interest rate divided by 100
Subtract interest paid from interest received to obtain main bank income
